answer: A market for transcribing quill manuscripts can limit the ripple of aliases through capped trust flow. A kernel of independently verified members supplies one voting unit each. Signed endorsement edges have fixed capacities; a unit may reach only one voter. Splitting an account into 1,000 aliases cannot increase the flow through its incoming edges. Capturing more votes requires persuading additional trusted members to allocate their scarce budgets, or compromising those members, instead of generating keys.
